name: Kamahl
title: From Pit Fighter to Druid
summary: A celebrated warrior whose pursuit of the Mirari led to tragedy, remorse, and a new calling as a protector of Krosa.
biography: Kamahl began as a formidable Pardic barbarian and gladiator, drawn to Cabal City and the Mirari during the struggle for power on Otaria. He befriended Chainer while competing in the Cabal pits; after Chainer lost control of the Mirari and his nightmares, Kamahl was forced to end his friend’s suffering.
The Mirari amplified his aggression. With the artifact bound to his sword, he seriously injured his sister Jeska, setting in motion her transformation into Phage.

Kamahl sought a different life in the Krosan Forest, where Thriss the Nantuko taught him druidic ways. His transformation from pit fighter to protector would shape the Onslaught story and his efforts to save Jeska.

The Cabal pits turned his skill into public acclaim, but he also formed a genuine friendship with Chainer, whose training and loyalties were unlike his own. Chainer’s fall left Kamahl with a memory of violence that could not be understood merely as victory over an opponent.

The Mirari did not invent Kamahl’s pride. It intensified his existing hunger for power until he tried to force the Pardic tribes to follow him and struck Jeska in a rage. His later remorse did not heal her or undo the political consequences of his conduct.

In Krosa, Kamahl studied with Thriss the Nantuko and redirected his strength toward the defense of the forest. Wizards later represented the historical contrast with red Kamahl, Pit Fighter and green Kamahl, Fist of Krosa; those are different phases of the same life, not independent legendary warriors.

His legacy survived him. Wizards' later biography of Kamahl, Heart of Krosa identifies the Kamahlite order of druids as an institution founded in Krosa to honor his life and actions. This later remembrance should not be mistaken for an organization that governed Kamahl during the Mirari crisis.

featuredCard.significance: A reprint of Kamahl's green incarnation, originally introduced in Onslaught to reflect his turn from violent pit fighting toward druidic magic.

source.title: Wizards of the Coast — Kamahl, Heart of Krosa
